events.title: Portugal Restores Its Independence
events.description: Portuguese nobles overthrew Spanish rule in Lisbon, and the Duke of Braganza was proclaimed King John IV. The coup ended 60 years of the Iberian Union, in which the two crowns shared a monarch.
events.significance: It started the Portuguese Restoration War and put the House of Braganza on the throne. Portugal still marks the day as a national holiday.

events.title: Dr Pepper Is First Served in Waco
events.description: The soft drink Dr Pepper was served for the first time at a drug store in Waco, Texas.
events.significance: It became one of America's oldest and best-known soft drinks.

events.title: Ford Introduces the Moving Assembly Line
events.description: The Ford Motor Company began using the first moving assembly line for car production. Cars now came to the workers instead of workers going to the cars.
events.significance: It sharply cut the time and cost of building a car. That made automobiles affordable to ordinary families and changed manufacturing around the world.

events.title: Rosa Parks Is Arrested in Montgomery
events.description: Seamstress Rosa Parks refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger in Montgomery, Alabama. She was arrested for violating the city's segregation laws.
events.significance: Her arrest set off the Montgomery bus boycott, a major turning point in the American Civil Rights Movement.

events.title: Channel Tunnel Workers Meet Under the Sea
events.description: British and French tunnelling crews broke through the rock between them, about 40 meters beneath the English Channel seabed. It was the first land link between Britain and continental Europe in thousands of years.
events.significance: The breakthrough was a milestone for the Channel Tunnel, which opened in 1994 and now carries high-speed rail between the two countries.
